sections.label: Road Traffic Act review timing
sections.summary: The Road Traffic Act's last comprehensive review was in 1996, making the 2019 Amendment Bill timely.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: While the RTA has been updated regularly, the last comprehensive review was conducted more than 20 years ago, in 1996.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Road Traffic (Amendment) Bill 2019 is, therefore, timely.

sections.label: Fatal accidents and feedback trends
sections.summary: Fatal road traffic accidents dropped over 20% in five years, while irresponsible driving feedback letters rose over 70%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, the number of fatal road traffic accidents has dropped more than 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The number of feedback letters received on irresponsible driving has increased by more than 70% in five years.

sections.label: Four levels of harm
sections.summary: Higher harm caused by a motorist brings higher punishment, with four levels: Death, Grievous Hurt, Hurt and Endangering Life.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: If the motorist causes more harm, the level of punishment will be higher.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: There will be four levels of harm: Death, Grievous Hurt, Hurt and Endangering Life.

sections.label: Penalties for Dangerous Driving causing Death
sections.summary: First-time offenders face up to eight years' jail, repeat offenders up to 15, plus minimum disqualification, suspension and vehicle forfeiture.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: With these changes, for Dangerous Driving causing Death, a first-time offender will be liable for up to eight years of imprisonment, up from five years at present.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Repeat offenders will now be liable for up to 15 years of imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In addition, a first-time or repeat offender could also face a minimum DQ period of 10 years as well as immediate suspension and forfeiture of vehicle.

sections.label: Drink-and-drive causing death penalties
sections.summary: Drink-and-drive causing death brings added jail and disqualification, with repeat offenders facing up to 19 years and lifetime disqualification.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For example, a first-time offender who causes death by Dangerous Driving and had done so while driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs will face an additional maximum jail term of two years, and an additional minimum DQ period of two years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This means that motorists who drink-and-drive and cause death by Dangerous Driving will now be liable for a maximum jail term of 10 years, and to a minimum DQ period of at least 12 years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Repeat offenders will likewise face higher penalties of up to 19 years in jail and lifetime disqualification from driving.

sections.label: Minimum jail for first-time offenders
sections.summary: A first-time offender for Dangerous Driving causing Death will be jailed for at least two years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: With the changes, a first-time offender for Dangerous Driving causing Death will be jailed for at least two years.

sections.label: Fines for errant road users
sections.summary: Composition fines for traffic violations by pedestrians and cyclists were raised, and dangerous acts causing harm should not go lightly punished.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For example, the composition fines for traffic violations by pedestrians and cyclists were raised recently.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Engagement and education do help to rehabilitate errant road users.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: However, where an act is dangerous and causes harm to others, we should not let it go lightly punished.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Doing so will only undermine our road safety regime.

sections.label: Licence suspension and revocation measures
sections.summary: Four measures cover streamlining suspension and revocation, longer suspension for repeat offenders, revoking all probationary licences, and past compounded offences as aggravating factor.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: First, to streamline the licence suspension and revocation process; second, to lengthen the licence suspension period for repeat offenders; third, to revoke all of an individual's probationary licences, as long as any one of them is revoked; and fourth, to allow the Courts to consider past compounded road traffic offences as an aggravating factor for the purposes of sentencing a person convicted of a road traffic offence.

sections.label: Deputy Commissioner licence suspension powers
sections.summary: The RTA will be amended so the Deputy Commissioner of Police can effect licence suspension or revocation four weeks from notice to the motorist.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To allow them to continue driving while they drag out the appeal process is to put other motorists at risk.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will amend the RTA to make it clear that the Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) is allowed to effect licence suspension or revocation four weeks from the date of its notice to the affected motorist.

sections.label: Longer licence suspension periods
sections.summary: The RTA will be amended to let Traffic Police suspend a licence for up to five years, from up to three years currently.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Upon successfully passing the course, motorists will have their suspension periods reduced significantly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We propose to amend the RTA to allow Traffic Police to suspend an individual’s licence for up to five years, from up to three years currently.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For instance, with the change, motorists who are facing their sixth suspension, which is equivalent to accumulating demerit points from at least seven red-light beating offences in a short span of time, will have their licence suspended for four years.

sections.label: Suspension length by previous suspensions
sections.summary: Subsidiary legislation will stipulate suspension length based on the number of previous suspensions, with seven such motorists in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Subsidiary legislation will be prescribed to stipulate the length of the suspension period based on the number of previous suspensions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In 2018 alone, there were seven such motorists.

sections.label: Past compounded offences as aggravating factor
sections.summary: The fourth measure allows Courts to consider past compounded road traffic offences as an aggravating factor when sentencing a person convicted of a road traffic offence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The fourth measure is to allow the Courts to consider past compounded road traffic offences as an aggravating factor for the purpose of sentencing a person convicted of a road traffic offence.

sections.label: Helmet penalty raised
sections.summary: Penalties for riding without a helmet will be raised to match other Road Traffic Act offences, which carry up to three months' jail and a $1,000 fine.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This penalty is less severe than those of other similar offences in the RTA, such as failing to wear a proper seat belt or making an illegal U-turn, which attract a jail term of up to three months and a fine of up to $1,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will raise the penalties for riding without a helmet to the same level.

sections.label: Road Traffic Amendment Bill purpose
sections.summary: The Road Traffic (Amendment) Bill prevents and deters road traffic offences and calibrates punishment to achieve more accurate justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These real-life stories drive home the importance of driving responsibly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Road Traffic (Amendment) Bill prevents and deters road traffic offences as well as calibrates the punishment to achieve a more accurate form of justice in the particular situation.

sections.label: Drink-driving disqualification periods
sections.summary: Amended section 67(2) provides two years' disqualification for first drink-driving offenders and five years for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Every month for the first nine months of 2018, one person lost his or her life to an accident related to drink-driving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Although the number of persons arrested for drink-driving decreased by 3.7% in 2018 compared to 2017, if I am not mistaken, the number of drink-driving accidents increased by 17.3%, with the proportion of motorcyclists increasing by 51.3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Instead of a minimum period of 12 months disqualification, the amended section 67(2) provides for two years for a first offender and five years for repeat offenders.

sections.label: Penalties for unspecified offences
sections.summary: Clause 2 raises penalties under section 131 to fines up to $10,000 and/or three years' jail for first offences, and up to $20,000 and/or six years for subsequent offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: According to section 131, the penalty for offences without a specified penalty would be a fine not exceeding $1,000 and/or imprisonment not exceeding three months for the first offence and a fine not exceeding $2,000 and/or imprisonment not exceeding six months for subsequent offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A lot of "not exceeding" in that sentence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But clause 2 of the Bill raises the penalty for these offences to a fine of up to $10,000 and/or imprisonment not exceeding three years for the first offence and a fine of up to $20,000 and/or imprisonment up to six years for subsequent offences.

sections.label: Calibrating punishment by culpability
sections.summary: The Bill calibrates punishment according to culpability, aggravating factors, gravity of hurt caused, and whether the offender is recalcitrant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Bill calibrates it according to culpability, aggravating factor of drink-driving or some other serious offence, gravity of hurt caused, and whether or not the offender is recalcitrant.

sections.label: Compounded offences for sentencing
sections.summary: New section 139AA, clause 21, allows compounded offences to be taken into consideration for sentencing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Another way this Bill allows punishment to be better calibrated is by providing for compounded offences to be taken into consideration for sentencing in the new section 139AA, clause 21 of this Bill.

sections.label: Bus captain monitoring and standards
sections.summary: The bus captain's experience, schedule, hours, breaks and shift duration were within mandated industry standards, and a telematics system monitors every journey.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They were able to account for the bus captain's years of experience, driving schedule, daily working hours, break times and shift duration, all of which were well within mandated industry standards.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They also shared with me their company's proprietary telematics system that monitors every bus captain for every journey, tracking data, such as their driving and turning speeds and instances of sudden braking.

sections.label: Bus captain suspended after accident
sections.summary: After the accident, the bus captain was immediately suspended once the investigation found he was at fault and the bus had no issues.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: After my accident, the bus captain was immediately suspended when the investigation established that he was at fault and that there were no issues with the bus.

sections.label: Discretionary right-turn lanes discontinued
sections.summary: The speaker wants to examine discretionary right-turn lanes and is heartened that LTA plans to discontinue most such junctions within five years.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I, therefore, wish to delve more deeply into the issue of discretionary right-turn lanes.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am heartened that LTA has concrete plans to discontinue most discretionary right-turn junctions within the next five years.

sections.label: Right-turn junction accidents and fatalities
sections.summary: In 2016, Minister Khaw Boon Wan revealed 14 fatalities and 319 injuries from 2011 to 2015 at right-turn junctions, and Mdm Salimah Mohamad was killed in February.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2016, the hon Member Dr Chia Shi-Lu had inquired about accidents at right-turn lanes and, in his reply, Minister Khaw Boon Wan revealed that between 2011 and 2015, there were a total of 14 fatalities and 319 injuries involving pedestrians and cyclists being hit by right-turning vehicles at such junctions.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, in February this year, policewoman Mdm Salimah Mohamad was killed by a car turning right at such a junction in Shenton Way when the driver failed to keep a proper lookout.

sections.label: Safety enhancements and shorter timeline urged
sections.summary: LTA introduced safety enhancements like traffic light timings and Silver Zones, but the speaker urges shortening the five-year timeline for discontinuing discretionary right-turn junctions.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: LTA has introduced various safety enhancements to such junctions, including traffic light timings that give pedestrians a head-start in crossing the road and Silver Zones where speed limits are lowered to cater to the large number of senior citizens in these areas.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I would like to urge LTA to shorten the timeline for discontinuing these discretionary right-turn junctions from the projected five years, so that more accidents and fatalities can be prevented.

sections.label: Stiffer penalties for reckless driving
sections.summary: The RTA Bill will introduce stiffer penalties for reckless driving to encourage drivers to be more mindful and conscientious.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The RTA Bill will notably introduce stiffer penalties for reckless driving that will encourage drivers to be more mindful and conscientious.

sections.label: Traffic accidents, feedback and summonses
sections.summary: Accidents declined between 2014 and 2018, but Traffic Police feedback more than doubled from 6,900 to 18,500, and summonses rose from 152,700 to 181,000 between 2015 and 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Although the number of accidents have declined between 2014 and 2018, the number of feedback received by the Traffic Police about irresponsible drivers have more than doubled, from 6,900 to 18,500.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Between 2015 and 2018, the number of summonses issued has increased from 152,700 to 181,000.

sections.label: Drink-driving accidents increase
sections.summary: Drink-driving accidents increased by 17.3% to 176 cases last year, from 150 in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The number of drink-driving accidents increased by 17.3% to 176 cases last year, from 150 in 2017.

sections.label: Red-light running violations spike
sections.summary: The number of red-light running violations spiked by 15.7% to 53,910 cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The number of red-light running violations spiked by 15.7% to 53,910 cases.

sections.label: Rehabilitating bad behaviour early, DIPS
sections.summary: The speaker suggests efforts to rehabilitate bad behaviour early and asks whether the DIPS programme could be enhanced to give drivers more specific support and motivation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Perhaps there could also be efforts in rehabilitating bad behaviour very early on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I believe that DIPS was one good way to encourage good behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Could there perhaps be some enhancements to this programme to provide more specific support and motivation to these drivers?

sections.label: Zipper rule for merging traffic
sections.summary: The speaker is unsure if many Singaporean drivers follow the zipper rule, under which merging drivers from the left and right alternately give way so traffic flows smoothly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: For example, I am not sure if many Singaporean drivers follow the "zipper rule".

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: According to the rule, when traffic merges, drivers merging from the left and right should alternately give way to one another so that traffic flows smoothly.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill, which covers more road offences and issues harsher punishments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the above, I stand in support of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to do so through covering more road offences and issuing harsher punishments.

sections.label: Notice of Offence demerit points
sections.summary: Residents and workers driving for a living said Notice of Offence letters should state demerit points and the remaining threshold before licence suspension or revocation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My residents and workers driving for a living also shared that it will be a useful reminder if the current Notice of Offence letters can also state the number of demerit points generated by the individual driver as well as the remaining threshold before suspension or revocation of licence kicks in.

sections.label: Black Spot Programme safety measures
sections.summary: Under the Black Spot Programme, accident-prone locations are identified and safety measures such as special signs and clearer road markings are implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, under the Black Spot Programme, accident-prone locations are identified and safety measures, such as special signs and clearer road markings, are implemented.

sections.label: Rebates for vehicle safety technologies
sections.summary: It asks whether the Traffic Police or LTA can work with vehicle fleet owners to consider rebates when owners install safety-enabling technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To increase the level of road safety and adoption, can the Traffic Police or LTA work together with vehicle fleet owners to consider perhaps things like rebates when a vehicle owner installs safety-enabling technologies in their vehicles?

sections.label: WHO global road fatality rates
sections.summary: The WHO's 2018 report gave an average global road traffic fatality rate of 18.2 per 100,000 in 2016, while Singapore's was 2.51 in 2016 and 2.2 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the 2018 Global Status Report on Road Safety, the World Health Organization (WHO) reported that the average global road traffic fatality rate per 100,000 people was 18.2 in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore’s fatality rate was 2.51 in 2016 and has since improved to 2.2 in 2018.

sections.label: Traffic offence fines revised April 2019
sections.summary: Traffic offence fines were recently revised in April 2019 as part of the same review that led to the Bill's amendments to the RTA.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As part of the same review that led to this Bill's amendments to the RTA, traffic offence fines were recently revised in April 2019.

sections.label: Israel red-light fine increase effects
sections.summary: Red-light violations in Israel fell by 30% after the fine was increased, with young drivers and drivers with newer cars responding differently.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Overall, red-light violations in Israel fell by 30% after the fine was increased.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Young drivers, those aged under 30, were more than twice as likely as older drivers to reduce offending, although young drivers offend more to begin with.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And drivers with newer cars were both more likely to run red lights and they were less responsive to the fine increase.

sections.label: Finland speeding fine reported
sections.summary: The New York Times reported in 2015 that a Finnish businessman was fined €54,024 for driving 64 miles/h in a 50 mile/h zone.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2015, the New York Times reported that a businessman in Finland received a fine of €54,024 for exceeding the speed limit by traveling 64 miles/h in a 50 mile/h zone.

sections.label: Scaling fines by vehicle value
sections.summary: One practical way might be to scale the traffic fine based on the offending vehicle's Open Market Value for privately-owned passenger cars.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One practical way of doing so might be to scale the traffic fine based on the offending vehicle's Open Market Value, for privately-owned passenger cars.

sections.label: Removing animal definition
sections.summary: The Bill proposes to remove the definition of "animal" under section 84(6), creating a catch-all provision for a driver's obligation to stop after an accident involving an animal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes to remove the definition of "animal" under section 84(6).

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This creates a catch-all provision in relation to a driver's obligation to stop in the event of an accident involving an animal.

sections.label: New section 139AA after ruling
sections.summary: The new section 139AA comes in the wake of the High Court decision in Public Prosecutor vs Koh Thiam Huat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, the new section 139AA comes in the wake of the High Court decision in Public Prosecutor vs Koh Thiam Huat.

sections.label: Composition effect and section 139AA
sections.summary: Mr Wong Kan Seng explained in May 2015 that composition means the alleged offender is taken not to have been convicted, and the Minister is asked to confirm section 139AA will not change that position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In May 2015, during the Second Reading speech for the Parliamentary Elections (Amendment) Bill, then Minister for Home Affairs, Mr Wong Kan Seng, explained that the legal effect of composition is that "the alleged offender is taken not to have been convicted of the offence." Can the Minister confirm that the new section 139AA will not have the effect of changing the existing legal position that compounding an offence, whether under RTA, the Penal Code or other statutes, amounts to an acquittal?

sections.label: Composition versus conviction differences
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to clarify the remaining practical differences between composition and conviction under the RTA, whether section 139AA states general composition principles beyond the RTA, and whether compoundable offences can be taken into account for sentencing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Government is absolutely committed to upholding the presumption of innocence as a core principle in our commitment to the Rule of Law.” Can the Minister clarify what the remaining practical differences are between a composition and a conviction under the RTA?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Further, can the Minister clarify if the new section 139AA is intended to be a statement of the general legal principles of composition beyond the RTA?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In other words, is it the case that compoundable offences, whether under the RTA or other statutes, can be taken into account for the purpose of sentencing?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Judge in the case of re Lim Chor Pee noted that, “There are multiple reasons why a person may wish to compound an offence, whether it be an income tax offence or an offence compoundable under the Penal Code, without any admission of guilt.” Hypothetically, an individual who has been charged but had not, in fact, committed the offence may agree to pay the composition fee and dispose of the matter out of expediency.

sections.label: Extra punishment for serious offenders
sections.summary: Proposed sections 64 and 65 add punishment beyond dangerous driving, raising the possibility of double punishment for serious offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under the proposed sections 64 and 65, if the same person is convicted for dangerous driving or careless driving, he is subject to an extra punishment which is in addition to the punishment for dangerous driving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, for example, under the proposed section 64(2)(b), if hurt is caused, where an offender is a serious offender, he is to be punished with a fine of not less than $2,000 and not more than $10,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than 12 months or to both, in addition to the punishment for dangerous driving charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: On the face of it, there is a possibility that the serious offender may be punished twice.

sections.label: Parity of drink-driving sentences
sections.summary: Section 67(1) drink-driving and section 69(4) refusing a breath specimen currently carry parity of sentence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Currently, there is a parity of sentence under section 67(1), which deals with drink-driving, and under section 69(4) of the RTA, which deals with refusing to give a breath specimen for a preliminary breath test.

sections.label: Enhanced drink-driving sentencing provisions
sections.summary: The Bill enhances sentencing for section 67(1) but not section 69(4), and a repeat refusal leads to a drink-driving charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the Bill, the sentencing provisions for section 67(1) are proposed to be enhanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, the same is not proposed for section 69(4) of the RTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If he again refuses to provide the breath sample, he will be presumed to have committed the offence of drink-driving and charged separately for that offence.

sections.label: Roadside breathalysers and ignition interlocks
sections.summary: The passage notes mobile roadside breathalysers give earlier readings and that France requires ignition interlocks for repeat drink-drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The motorist has to be transported to the Police station for this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Now, there are Police-grade mobile prescribed breathalyser machines readily available which provide very accurate readings and can be administered at the roadside.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What we will then get is a reading of the alcohol level of the motorist at an earlier time, which probably will be a better gauge of what his alcohol level was at the time he was driving or was in charge of his vehicle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I also note that in France, drink-drivers, especially repeat offenders, would be required to fit their cars with vehicle ignition breathalysers or ignition interlock which require them to take a test before they can start their car.

sections.label: Compulsory rear view cameras
sections.summary: The passage states that in the US, installing rear view cameras is compulsory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, in the US, it is compulsory to install rear view cameras.

sections.label: Penalties for dangerous driving
sections.summary: The passage cites a 2013 fine and five-year suspension and supports mandatory minimum jail sentences and immediate licence revocation.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In this case, the driver was fined $8,000 and suspended for five years and that happened in 2013, which means he got to drive again since last year.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The penalties for dangerous driving are simply disproportionate to the impact of their actions.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: That is why I agree with the proposed amendments for new mandatory minimum jail sentences to penalise dangerous and careless driving that cause death and grievous hurt.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope they will deter people from driving dangerously.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I also commend the change of law to immediately revoke the licences of people charged with dangerous driving, those with previous offences and those doing illegal racing.

sections.label: Motorist summonses increase 2015 to 2018
sections.summary: Summonses issued to motorists rose from 152,700 in 2015 to 181,000 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The number of summonses issued to motorists increased from 152,700 in 2015 to 181,000 in 2018.

sections.label: Rising summonses and road safety concerns
sections.summary: Summonses rose by 30,000 from 2015 to 2018 despite enforcement and education measures, with drink-driving accidents up 17% and red-light running offences up 16%.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Compared to 2015, there are 30,000 more summonses in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Half of the motorists said that they feel the roads are getting more unsafe.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: People waiting at the bus stops also feel that it is no longer safe to wait at a bus stop.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can do something to reverse this trend.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Despite recent measures, such as more intense enforcement, the installation of more red-light and speed cameras, new and ongoing public education and engagement initiatives, the number of summonses issued for motorist offences has gone up, from over 150,000 in 2015 to more than 180,000 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last year, the number of drink-driving accidents went up by 17%, and red-light running offences also increased by 16%.

sections.label: RAG arrows at all junctions
sections.summary: The speaker wants RAG signalling at all junctions, not most, and no vehicle turning when pedestrians may cross.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While I am heartened by LTA’s announcement last April to introduce Red-Amber-Green (RAG) arrows at most junctions by 2023, where drivers have to wait for the arrow to turn green before making a turn, I think it is important that all, not most, but all junctions should have RAG signalling and, when pedestrians may cross, no vehicles should be permitted to turn.

sections.label: Elderly pedestrian jaywalking accidents
sections.summary: The Traffic Police noted that 25% of all accidents involving pedestrians involve elderly pedestrians who jaywalk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Traffic Police had noted in their 2018 Traffic Accident Situation news release that accidents involving elderly pedestrians who jaywalk remain a concern, as 25% of all accidents involving pedestrians involve our elderly pedestrians.

sections.label: 2018 road traffic accident report
sections.summary: The Police report showed fewer road traffic accidents in 2018 but more fatal accidents than 2017, plus increases in drink-driving accidents and red-light running violations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: According to the annual road traffic accident situation report issued by the Singapore Police Force, while there were fewer road traffic accidents in 2018, the number of fatal road accidents had increased when compared with 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Police also noted an increase in the number of drink-driving accidents, as well as red-light running violations and related accidents.

sections.label: Culpability for aiding drink-driving
sections.summary: The speaker proposes that those who knowingly assist drink-driving, such as handing a drunk person car keys, be culpable of aiding and abetting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Currently, the proposed measures in the Bill only target the driver.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I propose that those who knowingly assist incidents of drink-driving, such as handing a drunk person the keys to the car, should also be made culpable of aiding and abetting drink-driving under the law.

sections.label: Ignition-interlock devices for drink-driving offenders
sections.summary: The speaker suggests mandating ignition-interlock devices in vehicles owned or driven by past drink-driving offenders to lower repeat incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Such devices would help lower incidents of drink-driving, especially by repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, like to suggest that we emulate this by mandating the installation of such ignition-interlock devices for vehicles owned or driven by past drink-driving offenders.

sections.label: Separating buses from cyclists
sections.summary: The speaker says bus drivers cannot pass cyclists within bus lanes and calls for separating buses from bicycles beyond raising penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Many bus drivers that I have spoken to, tell me that it is very difficult to manoeuvre the big bus past a cyclist, more so if it is a group of cyclists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is obvious that it is practically not possible to keep the bus within the bus lane and get past the cyclists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Let us, therefore, separate the big bus from the small bicycle before we end up with another tragic accident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, we can only accomplish so much just by raising penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We need to go beyond our business-as-usual mentality and relook at some of our previously held assumptions and conclusions regarding road safety.

sections.label: Unregulated PMDs and accident rates
sections.summary: Unregulated PMDs led to high accident rates, with 2,500 active mobility offences from May to December 2018, despite a footpath speed limit cut.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Previously, unregulated PMDs led to persistently high accident rates, with 2,500 active mobility offences recorded between May and December 2018 alone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Fifteen Town Councils then said that they would not rule out banning PMDs from void decks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is despite recent regulatory reductions of the speed limit of PMDs on footpaths from 15 km/h to 10 km/h.

sections.label: AVs in near-term mobility plans
sections.summary: AVs feature in near-term mobility plans as dynamically routed services to be piloted in Punggol, Tengah and Jurong Innovation District by 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: AVs feature in our near-term future mobility plans as dynamically routed services to be piloted in Punggol, Tengah and the Jurong Innovation District by 2022, a mere three years away.

sections.label: Testing locations so far
sections.summary: Testing has so far taken place at one-north, university campuses and Gardens-by-the-Bay.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Testing has so far been at one-north, university campuses as well as Gardens-by-the-Bay.

sections.label: Elderly in future AV trials
sections.summary: Entities involved in testing could be required to explore locations and methods to include the elderly in future trials.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Entities involved in testing could be required to explore locations and methods to ensure the elderly are part of the testing population in future trials.

sections.label: Learning from PMDs for AVs
sections.summary: The speaker says lessons from PMDs should inform AVs by involving elderly and vulnerable populations early.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Perhaps, Mr Deputy Speaker, I am pre-empting the new Point-to-Point Passenger Transport Industry Bill that has just been tabled for First Reading today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I think it is safe to say that we must learn from what we have experienced with PMDs by involving the elderly and vulnerable populations early on with AVs.

sections.label: More unlicensed driving cases caught
sections.summary: Traffic Police caught more motorists driving without valid licences, rising from 921 in 2014 to 1,435 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Traffic Police have been catching more motorists driving without valid licences in the last few years, from 921 in 2014, to 1,435 in 2018, and there are probably quite a number who got away, considering the difficulty of detection.

sections.label: Forfeiture as deterrent punishment
sections.summary: The speaker says such punishment may deter more effectively and be easier to enforce, noting the Bill's vehicle forfeiture offences.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And while this is an unpalatable measure, such a punishment may be a more effective deterrent and much easier to enforce.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I note that, already in this Bill, there is a range of offences which can result in the forfeiture of vehicles, for example, dangerous driving causing death or grievous hurt.

sections.label: EU mandatory safety measures by 2022
sections.summary: The EU will introduce other safety measures that will be mandatory by 2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The EU will also be introducing other safety measures which will be mandatory by 2022.

sections.label: Cognitive tests for elderly motorists
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to consider more stringent, frequent cognitive tests and health checks for elderly motorists.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Therefore, I urge the Ministry to consider implementing perhaps more stringent and frequent cognitive tests and health checks for all elderly motorists.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: These assessments should be annual or perhaps bi-annual for those aged 75 and above, as functional health can potentially decline steeply from this age.

sections.label: DCP notice period for retraining
sections.summary: The DCP can extend the suspension notice period, but only for the suspended motorist to attend the DIPS Retraining Course.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The DCP can extend the notice period for suspension, but only for the suspended motorist to attend the DIPS Retraining Course.

sections.label: Animal welfare and road safety
sections.summary: The Bill obligates the motorist to stop only when it is safe to do so, balancing animal welfare and road user safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We will have to balance between animal welfare and the safety of road users.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: That is why the Bill obligates the motorist to stop only when it is safe to do so.

sections.label: Drive Safe, Work Safe campaign
sections.summary: Under the Workplace Safety and Health Council's Drive Safe, Work Safe campaign, more than 200 heavy vehicle fleet owners pledged to implement safe driving measures for employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Under the Workplace Safety and Health Council's Drive Safe, Work Safe campaign, more than 200 heavy vehicle fleet owners have pledged to implement measures to encourage safe driving by their employees.

sections.label: Simulator training for learner motorists
sections.summary: The Traffic Police regularly update the driving course curriculum, and reviews led to introducing simulator training for all new learner motorists towards the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The Traffic Police regularly update the driving course curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: It is through these reviews that we have decided to introduce simulator training for all new learner motorists towards the end of the year.

sections.label: Medical examinations for older motorists
sections.summary: Motorists above 65 must undergo and pass a medical examination every three years, while heavy vehicle drivers must do so every year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Motorists above the age of 65 are required to undergo and pass a medical examination every three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Heavy vehicle drivers have added responsibilities and are required to do so every year.

sections.label: MHA study of similar system
sections.summary: MHA will study the suitability and impact of implementing a similar system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: MHA will study the suitability and impact of implementing a similar system.

sections.label: MHA consideration of suggestions
sections.summary: MHA will consider these suggestions with the relevant agencies for future reviews.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: MHA will consider these suggestions with the relevant agencies for future reviews.

sections.label: Sleep-deprived driving as aggravating factor
sections.summary: Courts have ruled that driving while sleep-deprived can be an aggravating factor in sentencing.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: On driving while sleep-deprived, the Courts have ruled that doing so can be considered as an aggravating factor in sentencing.

sections.label: Mechanical failure not dangerous driving
sections.summary: Mechanical failure of a vehicle is not classified as dangerous or careless driving as the fault is not linked to the manner of driving.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: On Er Dr Lee Bee Wah's second example of mechanical failure of a vehicle, this will not be classified as a dangerous nor careless driving offence, as the mechanical fault is not linked to the manner of driving.

sections.label: Motorist not liable if no time to react
sections.summary: A motorist who abides by traffic rules and still knocks into a victim who appeared suddenly with insufficient time to react is not liable for an irresponsible driving offence.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If the motorist had abided by the traffic rules, for example, keeping within speed limits and checking clear before making turns or changing lanes and yet still knock into the victim, for example, a PMD rider or jaywalker, because the latter had appeared suddenly on the road and left him with insufficient time to react, the motorist will not be liable for an irresponsible driving offence.

sections.label: Dangerous or careless driving while under influence
sections.summary: A motorist also driving dangerously or carelessly is liable under Dangerous or Careless Driving instead of Driving Under Influence per se, but driving dangerously or carelessly while under influence carries higher penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If he was also committing the second action, that is, driving dangerously or carelessly, he would be liable for penalties under Dangerous or Careless Driving instead of Driving Under Influence per se.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: However, the offence of driving dangerously or carelessly while under influence carries higher penalties.

sections.label: Illegal speed trial and dangerous driving charges
sections.summary: A motorist can be charged for both Dangerous or Careless Driving and Illegal Speed Trial.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Given the lower penalties for illegal speed trials, he asked if it will be the case that the prosecution will have to choose between forfeiting the vehicle for an illegal speed trial offence as opposed to the higher penalties for a Dangerous Driving offence.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is possible for a motorist to be charged for both the offence of Dangerous or Careless Driving and the offence of Illegal Speed Trial.

sections.label: Offence and offender meeting CPC requirements
sections.summary: The answer is yes if the offence and offender meet requirements under the CPC, such as not having a specified or mandatory minimum imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The answer is yes, if the offence and offender meet the requirements set out under the CPC, such as not having a specified or mandatory minimum imprisonment.

sections.label: Composition as aggravating factor
sections.summary: New section 139AA lets Courts treat composition of an offence as a possible aggravating factor when sentencing for a later RTA offence.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The new section 139AA makes it clear that the Courts may take the composition of an offence as a possible aggravating factor when a Court sentences for a later RTA offence.

sections.label: Compositions and criminal records
sections.summary: Compositions carry typically lower penalties and will not be considered part of an individual's criminal records.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Apart from the typically lower penalties for compositions, compositions will also not be considered as part of an individual’s criminal records.

sections.label: Findings on road user attitudes
sections.summary: Findings state road users prioritise their own needs, rate others' safety and graciousness negatively, and feel others should make roads safer.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: First, road users tend to prioritise their own needs to get to their destinations at the fastest speed and the shortest time possible.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Second, as highlighted by Ms Rahayu Mahzam, most road users rate their personal safety and graciousness positively, but rate the personal safety and graciousness of other road users negatively.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The third finding, unsurprisingly, is that the road users tend to feel that it is the responsibility of others to make the road safer.

sections.label: Road safety situation stable
sections.summary: The road safety situation remains stable and the number of road traffic accidents has decreased.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The road safety situation remains stable and the number of road traffic accidents has decreased.

sections.label: Court discretion for lower sentences
sections.summary: Clause 13's amendment allows Courts discretion to impose a sentence lower than the minimum mandatory sentence if there are special reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The amendment in clause 13 is to allow for the Courts to have discretion to deviate from and impose a sentence lower than the minimum mandatory sentence if there are special reasons to do so.
